headline: Clinton order keeps a presidential advisory committee on intellectual disabilities in place and expands its membership and duties.
what_it_does: This executive order continues the President's Committee on Mental Retardation, an advisory group to the President. It adds more members to the committee and gives it a broader set of responsibilities. Only the title is available, so the specific new members and duties are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: People with intellectual disabilities and their families
who_it_affects.how: The committee advises the President on issues that affect them, and it continues with a wider role.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the President's Committee on Mental Retardation
who_it_affects.how: The committee stays in operation with more members and more responsibilities.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed March 21, 1996; the exact effective date is not stated in the available information.
